title: Merz Cancels UN General Assembly Trip to Confront CDU Rebellion at Home
detail: Chancellor Friedrich Merz cancelled his planned trip to address the UN General Assembly's General Debate in New York — where the UN had scheduled his speech for the Wednesday after the September 20 Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern state elections — with his office saying 'contrary to original plans, the chancellor will not travel to New York next week, as his presence in Berlin is required.' The cancellation came amid what Der Spiegel described as a CDU 'palace revolt,' with senior CDU leaders set to meet the Monday after the vote and CDU/CSU Bundestag lawmakers meeting as a group two days later — sessions widely read as tests of Merz's leadership. Der Spiegel and other outlets reported open talk within the party of a 'Kanzlertausch' (chancellor swap), floating NRW premier Hendrik Wüst as a possible successor, though the CDU's eight state governors issued a joint statement backing Merz. An INSA poll for Bild published around September 13 found only 14% of Germans considered Merz fit for the chancellorship against 78% who did not — including a majority of the CDU's own voters.

media.caption: Chancellor Friedrich Merz cancels his UN General Assembly trip to remain in Berlin amid a CDU leadership crisis

title: AfD Hits Record 30% in GMS Nationwide Poll, 10 Points Ahead of CDU/CSU
detail: The GMS Institute's 'Sunday question' poll, published September 15 (fieldwork September 9–14, 1,009 respondents by phone and online panel), put the AfD at a record 30% nationally — up 2 points since late July — with the CDU/CSU falling 3 points to 20%, its lowest recorded GMS result. The Greens rose to 14% (+1), the Left to 11% (+1), the SPD held at 11%, the FDP fell to 4% (-1) and the BSW rose to 3% (+1), with the Free Voters at 1%. The poll landed five days before the Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern state elections and confirmed the national swing seen after the AfD's September 6 Saxony-Anhalt landslide; the sitting SPD/CDU coalition would not command a Bundestag majority if the poll were an election result.

media.caption: GMS Institute poll puts the AfD at a record 30% nationwide, 10 points ahead of the CDU/CSU
